questions.question: Vishal sells a bag at a profit of 40%. If Vishal's profit is Rs. 880, then what is the cost price of the bag?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Vishal sells a bag at a profit of 40%.

Vishal's profit is Rs. 880

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

40% = Rs. 880

⇒ 1% = 880/40

⇒ 100% = 2200

So, the cost price = Rs. 2200

**∴ The cost price of the bag is Rs. 2200.**

questions.question: A 900 metre long train crosses a 1200 metres long platform completely in 70 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A 900 metre long train crosses a 1200 metres long platform entirely in 70 seconds

**Concept used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

When a train crosses a platform, it will cover the length of its own + the length of the platform.

**Calculation:**

Total distance covered = 900 + 1200

⇒ 2100

Speed = 2100/70

⇒ 30 m/sec

Now,

Speed in km/h = 30 × (18/5)

⇒ 108

**∴ The speed of the train is 108 km/h.**

C.I = P(1 + R/100)T - P

P = Principal

R = Rate

T = Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ 12000(43/40)2 - 12000

⇒ 1867.5

questions.question: A 480 m long train takes 16 seconds to pass a pole. How long will it take to pass a platform that is 900 m long?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When speed is constant, Time is directly proportional to Distance.

Distance covered to cross a pole = 480 m

Distance covered to cross the platform = 480 + 900 = 1380 m

Ratio of distances = 480 : 1380 = 48 : 138 = 8 : 23

Time to cross platform = (16 ÷ 8) × 23 = 46 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 46 seconds.**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Time = Total Distance ÷ Speed

questions.question: If Rs. 1,000 is divided into three parts in the ratio 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 5, find the value of the smallest part.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rs. 1,000 is divided into three parts in the ratio 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 5

**Calculation:**

1st part = 1000 × 2/10

⇒ 200

2nd part = 1000 × 3/10

⇒ 300

3rd part = 1000 × 5/10

⇒ 500

So, smallest part = 200

**∴ The smallest part is Rs. 200.**

questions.question: Ishita can read a newspaper in 'n' minutes. What part of the newspaper can she read in 7 minutes? (n > 7)
questions.solution:

Ishita can read 7/nth part of a newspaper in 7 minutes.

**∴ The required answer is (7)/(n).**

questions.question: The base of a triangle is 16 cm and its area is 144 cm². Find its corresponding height, with respect to the given base.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The base of a triangle is 16 cm and its area is 144 cm2. 

**Concept used:**

Area of a base = 1/2 × base × height

**Calculation:**

1/2 × 16 × height = 144

⇒ 8 × height = 144

⇒ height = 18

**∴ The required answer is 18 cm.**

questions.question: A train moves at a speed of 35 km/h for the first 2 hours and at a speed of 50 km/h for the next 4 hours. Find the average speed of the train during the entire journey.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A train moves at a speed of 35 km/h for the first 2 hours and at a speed of 50 km/h for the next 4 hours.

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance/total time

**Calculation:**

Total distance = 2 × 35 + 4 × 50

⇒ 70 + 200

⇒ 270 km

Total time = 6 hours

Average speed = 270/6

⇒ 45 km/h

**∴ The average speed of the train during the entire journey is 45 km/h.**

questions.question: The selling price of two articles are equal. If the first article is sold at a profit of 20% and the second article is sold at a loss of 20%, what will be the overall loss percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

First article sold at = 20% profit

Second article sold at = 20% loss

**Concept used:**

CP = SP × 100/(100 + profit%)

CP = SP × 100/(100 - loss%)

**Calculation:**

Let the selling price be 120a

So, cost price of 1st item = 120a × (100/120)

⇒ 100a

Cost price of 2nd item = 120a × (100/80)

⇒ 150a

Total cost price = 100a + 150a

⇒ 250a

Total selling price = 240a

Loss = 10a

% of loss = (10a/250a) × 100

⇒ 4%

**∴ The required answer is 4%.**

questions.question: Rachit invests Rs. 12,000 for a 2-year period at a certain rate of simple interest per annum. Prasad invests Rs. 12,000 for a 2-year period at the same rate of interest per annum as Rachit, but in Prasad's case the interest is compounded annually. Find the rate of interest per annum if Prasad receives Rs. 172.80 more as interest than Rachit at the end of the 2-year period.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rachit invests Rs. 12,000 for a 2-year period at a certain rate of simple interest

Prasad invests Rs. 12,000 for a 2-year period at the same rate of interest per annum as Rachit, but in Prasad's case the interest is compounded annually.

Difference in interest is Rs. 172.8

**Concept used:**

Difference of C.I and S.I = P(R/100)²

**Calculation:**

Let the rate of interest be R

So,

172.8 = 12000 × (R/100)²

172.8 = 12000 × R²/10000

172.8 = 1.2 × R2

144 = R2

12 = R

So, rate of interest is 12%

**∴ The rate of interest is 12%.**

questions.question: In an office of 900 employees, on a particular day, except for 10% of the female employees, all employees were present. On the next day, except for 8% of the male employees, all employees were present. The number of employees present on each of these two days was the same. Find the total number of male employees on the payrolls of this office.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total employees = 900

**Calculation:**

Let total male female employees be 10M and 10F respectively.

According to the question,

⇒ 10M + 10F × (100 - 10)/100 = 10M × (100 - 8)/100 + 10F 

⇒ ⇒ 10M + 90F/100 = 92F/100 + 10F

⇒ 10M + 9F = 9.2M + 10F

⇒ 0.8M = 1F

⇒ M/F = 5/4

So, ratio of male and female = 5 : 4

So, total number of male = 900 × (5/9)

⇒ 500

**∴ The required answer is 500.**
